subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should durable wake systemEvent handoffs be bound to the session generation resolved for the wake, or intentionally survive a session reset into the replacement generation as part of the new durable-core contract?
rationale: Either behavior is implementable, but it changes user-visible session-state semantics and cannot safely be inferred from the queue implementation; the cumulative core runtime also requires explicit sponsorship.

options.title: Generation-bound delivery
options.body: Capture the resolved session ID, reject or re-resolve the queued wake after a generation mismatch, and add reset-race regression proof before considering the stack for merge.

options.title: Intentional cross-reset delivery
options.body: Document cross-reset systemEvent delivery as a durable-core contract and add tests proving authorization, ownership, transcript and deduplication behavior for replacement sessions.

options.title: Pause the durable stack
options.body: Keep the existing session-delivery queue behavior and defer this broader durable runtime until a maintainer sponsors its product and upgrade contract.

recommendation.title: Generation-bound delivery
recommendation.body: Capture the resolved session ID, reject or re-resolve the queued wake after a generation mismatch, and add reset-race regression proof before considering the stack for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans core architecture, persisted state, protocol surface and release policy rather than one isolated owner module.
